'''Wyndham John Albery''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}}<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hitchman |first1=Michael L. |last2=Bartlett |first2=Philip N. |date=2022 |title=Wyndham John Albery. 5 April 1936—3 December 2013 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=73|pages=13–39 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2022.0018 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (5 April 1936 – 3 December 2013) was a British physical chemist and academic.<ref name="telegraph">{{cite news| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/science-obituaries/10516978/Professor-John-Albery-obituary.html | title=Professor John Albery – obituary | newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] | location=UK | date=13 December 2013 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Wyndham John Albery was born on 5 April 1936. His father Michael James Albery (1910–75), a barrister, was part of a sprawling theatrical family network as the son of Gertrude Mary (née Jones, daughter of dramatist [[Henry Arthur Jones]]) and [[Irving Albery]] a Conservative MP and the son of actress and theatrical manager [[Mary Moore (stage actress)|Mary Moore]] (later Lady Wyndham) and dramatist [[James Albery]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winslow History {{!}} Silvanus Jones (1827-1914) and Henry Arthur Jones the playwright (1851-1929)|url=http://www.winslow-history.org.uk/winslow_families-jones.shtm|access-date=2021-10-02|website=www.winslow-history.org.uk}}</ref> His aunt [[Jessica Mary Albery]] was one of Britain's first female professional architects.<ref>{{Citation|last=Walker|first=Lynne|chapter=Albery, Jessica Mary (1908–1990), architect and town planner|date=2019-07-11|chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1093/odnb/9780198614128.013.112259|title=Oxford Dictionary of National Biography|publisher=Oxford University Press|doi=10.1093/odnb/9780198614128.013.112259|isbn=978-0-19-861412-8 |access-date=2021-10-02|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref>

He was educated at [[Winchester College]] and [[Balliol College, Oxford|Balliol College]], Oxford. He undertook his [[Doctor of Philosophy|D.Phil.]] at Oxford with [[Ronnie Bell (chemist)|Ronnie Bell]], starting in 1960.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.physchem.ox.ac.uk/history/solkin.htm | title=Kinetics in Solution | year=2007 | accessdate=23 May 2011 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070314092907/http://www.physchem.ox.ac.uk/history/solkin.htm | archivedate=14 March 2007}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Albery was appointed to a Weir Junior Research [[Fellow]]ship in October 1962 and then to a Fellowship and [[Praelectorship]] in [[Chemistry]] at [[University College, Oxford]] in October 1963, where he was briefly a colleague of [[E. J. Bowen]]. He served in his college as Junior Dean and Dean, and was Tutor for Admissions from 1968 to 1975. This period culminated in University College coming top of the [[Norrington Table]] in 1975.<ref name="univ-tribute">{{cite web | url=http://www.univ.ox.ac.uk/univ-news/tribute-former-master-professor-wyndham-john-albery | title=Tribute to former Master Professor Wyndham John Albery | date=3 December 2013 | publisher=[[University College, Oxford]] | accessdate=13 December 2013 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214063953/http://www.univ.ox.ac.uk/univ-news/tribute-former-master-professor-wyndham-john-albery | archivedate=14 December 2013 | df=dmy-all }}</ref>

Coming from the theatrical [[Albery family]], he was an enthusiastic senior member of the [[University College Players]], organiser of the [[Univ Revue]],<ref name="martlet14">{{cite news| title=In Memoriam: Professor John Albery | page =28 | date=Summer 2014 | journal=The Martlet | publisher=[[University College, Oxford]] }}</ref> held in the college Hall, and script-writer for [[Experimental Theatre Club]] revues staged by the Etceteras. Early in his career, in 1962, he wrote for ground-breaking [[BBC]] satirical comedy television show ''[[That Was The Week That Was]]''.<ref>{{IMDb name|id=0016797|name=John Albery}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/comedy/guide/talent/a/albery_john.shtml | title=John Albery | work=[[BBC]] Guide to Comedy | year=2006 | accessdate=23 May 2011 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060217024931/http://www.bbc.co.uk/comedy/guide/talent/a/albery_john.shtml | archivedate=17 February 2006}}</ref>

After [[Oxford]], Albery became Professor of Physical Chemistry from 1978 at [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{cite book| first=Hannah | last=Guy | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=x4u4ikoj1M8C&pg=PA548 | title=The history of Imperial College London, 1907–2007 | publisher=[[Imperial College Press]] | year=2007 | page=548 | isbn=9781860948183 }}</ref>

In 1989, he returned to Oxford to be [[Master (college)|Master]] of University College.<ref>{{cite news |title=The New Master | pages=14–15 | work=[[University College Record]]| publisher=[[University College, Oxford]] | date=October 1989}}</ref> He hosted the visit of President [[Bill Clinton]] (a former student of University College) and his wife [[Hillary Clinton]] to the college in June 1994.<ref name="symonds">{{cite book | title=The Changing Faces of North Oxford: Book Two | last=Symonds | first=Ann Spokes | year=1998 | publisher=[[Robert Boyd Publications]] | location=Witney | page=137 | isbn=1-899536-33-7}}</ref>

Albery subsequently became Barrer Fellow in Chemistry at Imperial College. He was a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1985, the first Master of University College to be so. He was an Honorary Fellow of University College, Oxford, and a celebration of his 75th birthday was held in Oxford in 2011.<ref>{{cite news | title=Varia | pages=134–136 | work=[[University College Record]]| publisher=[[University College, Oxford]] | date=October 2011 }}</ref>

Albery was a long-term collaborator of [[Jeremy R. Knowles|Jeremy Knowles]], and published many articles with him, for example in studying the energetics of the reaction catalysed by [[proline racemase]].<ref name="pmid3718964">{{cite journal|date=1986|title=Energetics and mechanism of proline racemase|journal=Biochemistry|volume=25|issue=9|pages=2572–7|doi=10.1021/bi00357a043|pmid=3718964|vauthors=Albery WJ, Knowles JR}}</ref>

==Later life==
He died of cancer on 3 December 2013.<ref name="univ-tribute" /> A memorial service was held at the [[University Church of St Mary the Virgin]] in Oxford on 5 April 2014 with tributes by [[Leslie Mitchell (historian)|Leslie Mitchell]] and Robert Hillman.<ref>{{citation| title=A Service of Thanksgiving for the life of John Albery FRS | publisher=[[University College, Oxford]] | location=University Church of St Mary the Virgin | date=5 April 2014 }}</ref>

==Books==
* ''Ring-Disc Electrodes'', with M. L. Hitchman, [[Oxford University Press]], 1971 ({{ISBN|0-19-855349-8}}).
* ''Electrode Kinetics'', Oxford University Press, 1975 ({{ISBN|0-19-855433-8}}).
